We have been offering complete kiln & furnace solutions for over 70 years. We’re proud to say that our products can be found operating in countries the world over, which is testament to both our products and our continual evolution as a company.  
Over the years, our product range has grown and developed in line with the latest technological innovations to meet the ever-changing demands of the industry. As well as our staple products and services that have helped cement our reputation as the UK’s premier kiln and furnace supplier, our range now encompasses the following:
  * Pottery kilns and equipment
  * Glass kilns
  * High Tech Ceramic kilns
  * Metal heat treatment furnaces
  * Dental furnaces
  * Many specialist heat treatment processes


Sustainability, Versatility & Innovation  
Versatility and innovation are the keystones of our business, along with a sustained policy of continuous improvement. Whilst the basic methods and processes behind our craft have remained unchanged for years, we now combine the wealth of in-depth knowledge we have accumulated over the years with the very latest in Computer Aided Design to ensure we stay at the forefront of kiln and furnace manufacturing.
Perfection through Dedication  
Every member of our valued team is passionate about striving for perfection. They dedicate their time to producing first class equipment that has to meet a myriad of different requirements; requirements which are dictated by the wide and growing range of clients we now serve, across both newly burgeoning and age-old industries.
Seal of Quality  
The Kilns & Furnaces symbol can be found all around the world. People working within our family of industries know it as a hallmark of quality. It symbolises an unwavering commitment to customer care and client-focused innovation.
Our Business is Driven by You  
Our customers are at the heart of what we do. We will gladly answer any of your questions regarding any of our products and services, so please get in touch with your queries, comments, suggestions or feedback.
Industrial Kilns & Furnaces  
At the heart of our business are our industrial kilns and industrial furnaces, engineered to deliver exceptional performance, precision, and reliability across a wide range of applications. From heat treatment and sintering to calcination and material testing, our systems are designed and built to meet the demanding requirements of modern manufacturing environments.
Each industrial furnace and industrial kiln is crafted using advanced Computer Aided Design and manufactured in the UK to the highest quality standards, ensuring long-term durability, energy efficiency, and consistent temperature control. Trusted by organisations around the world, Kilns & Furnaces continues to lead the industry in providing bespoke thermal processing solutions that combine technical innovation with over 70 years of engineering expertise.

## Brazing Furnaces
[Kilns & Furnaces](https://www.kilns.co.uk/) designs and manufactures advanced brazing furnaces for precision joining applications used across aerospace, automotive, medical, and general manufacturing sectors. Our systems deliver the controlled heat, clean atmospheres, and repeatable temperature profiles essential for producing strong, high-integrity brazed joints.
With more than 70 years of experience, we offer reliable, efficient solutions for industrial brazing, including specialist vacuum brazing furnace systems.
### **Industrial Furnaces for Brazing Applications**
Brazing requires accurate temperature control and a clean environment to ensure consistent wetting, minimal oxidation, and high joint strength. Our [industrial furnaces](https://www.kilns.co.uk/industrial-kilns-furnaces) are engineered to provide stable, uniform heat with precise control over process atmospheres.
We supply a full range of furnace types for industrial brazing, including **Vacuum Brazing Furnaces** , ideal for aerospace, medical, and high-precision engineering applications requiring oxide-free bonding and controlled diffusion. We also manufacture **Batch Brazing Furnaces** , which are flexible, highly controllable systems for multi-purpose industrial brazing workflows.
Each furnace is built for accurate thermal management, efficient energy use, and reliable long-term performance.
### **Brazing Applications & Capabilities**
Our brazing furnace systems support a broad spectrum of industrial joining processes:
  * **Vacuum Brazing** : Flux-free, contamination-free bonding for high-integrity components.
  * **Atmosphere Brazing** : Controlled gas environments for sensitive metals and assemblies.
  * **High-Volume Industrial Brazing** : Repeatable production for heat exchangers, automotive parts, and engineered assemblies.
  * **Post-Brazing Heat Treatments** : Stabilisation, stress relief, and conditioning cycles.
  * **Precision Brazed Components** : Suitable for stainless steel, superalloys, copper alloys, and specialised materials.


Furnaces can be equipped with multi-zone temperature control, automated loading, data logging, and integration with digital factory systems.
### **Engineered for Performance & Compliance**
All brazing furnaces comply with BS EN 746, CE, and UKCA standards. Advantages include clean, controlled atmospheres (vacuum or gas), energy-efficient insulation, long-life structural components, high temperature uniformity, full safety systems, and advanced digital controls
Each furnace is engineered around the customer’s chosen materials, filler metals, tolerances, and production requirements.
### **Why Choose Kilns & Furnaces?**
– Over 70 years of furnace design and manufacturing experience  
– Proven expertise in furnaces for vacuum brazing and industrial brazing  
– Custom furnace design for specific joint and material requirements  
– UK-based installation, support, and maintenance services
### **Bespoke Brazing Furnace Solutions**
Whether you require a specialist vacuum brazing furnace, a high-capacity continuous line, or a flexible batch brazing system, we can design a furnace tailored to your exact process specifications.
[Contact our engineering team](https://www.kilns.co.uk/contact-us) today for expert guidance or a bespoke quotation.

## Kiln Refurbishment Services
Kilns & Furnaces are your trusted partner for comprehensive kiln refurbishment services in the UK. With over 60 years of expertise in kiln design, manufacturing, maintenance, and refurbishment, we are committed to ensuring your kiln runs safely and efficiently.
* * *
### Expertise You Can Trust
Our company has over 60 years of successful trading, based in Stoke-on-Trent, our team of fully qualified experts offer a wealth of experience in refurbishing various types of electric and gas-fired kilns. Whether you have a rotary, intermittent, shuttle, or fixed hearth kiln, we have the knowledge and skills to bring it back to optimal performance.
### Comprehensive Kiln Parts and Services
As an industry leading kiln manufacturer, we offer a complete range of kiln parts to complete your refurbishment. We are able to refurbish all parts of your kiln, from replacement elements, insulation, and refractory bricks, restoring your kiln to optimise performance. We understand the intricacies of kiln systems and provide tailored solutions to meet your specific needs.
### Compliance and Safety Assurance
Our dedicated team ensures that your refurbished kiln complies with all relevant IEE regulations and aligns with current safety standards. Your safety and the efficiency of your kiln are our top priorities. You can trust us to deliver a refurbished kiln that not only meets industry standards but exceeds your expectations.
### Kiln Refurbishment Process
Custom Solutions: Tailored solutions are developed to address the unique needs of your kiln, ensuring optimal performance.
Quality Parts: We only use high-quality kiln parts in the refurbishment process.

## About Us
Tradition Meets Innovation
We put our many successful years of trading and growth down to our diverse team of dedicated professionals. Kilns & Furnaces Ltd is comprised of industry veterans and dynamic graduates alike, who bring a combination of experience and innovation to every project we take on. This means that you know each product you purchase from us offers trusted originality backed by years of hands-on, practical expertise.
Your Requirements, Our Speciality
Having built a solid foundation in the industry over 70 years ago, our commitment to continual improvement and diversification has allowed us to cement our place in the modern kiln and furnace manufacturing landscape.  
As a result we are now happy to offer a service that is not just tailored but personalised to the needs of your company. As our organisation has grown, so too have our popular product lines. From our individual hobby kilns and pottery equipment, to our globally renowned industrial furnaces, everything we offer is purpose-built and purpose-driven. As you will see throughout our extensive product ranges, research and requirement feed into the design of every product we manufacture, which ensures that the needs of real professionals in the industry rest at the forefront of our cutting-edge designs.  
A number of our highly satisfied clients also opt for our bespoke manufacture and design service, wherein we work together to come up with a complete kiln and furnace solution directly suited to their needs, eliminating unnecessary expenditure and thus increasing return on investment.
A Global Network
Operating out of our purpose built factory in the heart of England, our longstanding ethos of quality, efficiency and modernisation has allowed us to provide comprehensive kiln and furnace solutions to an ever expanding global market. Our catalogue of returning clientele consists of multinational corporations and individual potters alike, because we firmly believe that no project is too small or large for our dedicated team.  
Please take a look through our online catalogue, where we’re sure that, regardless of your size or budget, you’ll find a solution to all of your kiln and furnace needs. If you don’t find what you’re looking for, please get in touch today to discuss our highly acclaimed bespoke design and construction services.

## Sintering Furnaces
Sintering is a critical process in modern manufacturing, used to transform powdered materials into dense, high-strength components through carefully controlled heat treatment. At [Kilns & Furnaces](https://www.kilns.co.uk/), we design and build specialist sintering furnaces that provide the precise thermal environments required for consistent and reliable results across a wide range of industries.
Our systems are used in applications including technical ceramics, powder metallurgy, and [advanced engineered materials](https://www.kilns.co.uk/advanced-materials-manufacturing), where temperature accuracy and process control directly impact final product performance. Sintering kilns also play an important role in metal 3D printing, or additive manufacturing, where post-print sintering is required to achieve the density and mechanical properties needed for functional metal components.
Engineered to deliver stable, uniform heat throughout the chamber, our sintering kilns ensure even densification and minimising defects during processing. Accurate control of heating and cooling rates allows manufacturers to maintain strict process parameters, supporting improved material properties and repeatability. Each furnace is equipped with advanced control systems, high-performance insulation, and robust heating elements, enabling efficient operation at elevated temperatures while reducing energy consumption and thermal loss.
We understand that sintering processes can vary significantly depending on the material and application. Our furnaces can therefore be tailored to suit individual production requirements, including chamber size, temperature capability, and atmosphere control. Systems can be designed for batch or continuous operation, with options for multi-zone heating and full process monitoring.

## Materials Testing Furnaces
At [Kilns & Furnaces](https://www.kilns.co.uk/), we design and manufacture high-performance [materials testing kilns and furnaces](https://www.kilns.co.uk/kilns/test-kilns) for the precise evaluation of refractory and high-temperature materials. With over 70 years of engineering expertise, our systems provide controlled heating, consistent temperature profiles, and robust durability, enabling accurate materials testing across a wide range of industrial and research applications. Our solutions are used by manufacturers, laboratories, and quality assurance teams to ensure material performance, reliability, and compliance under extreme conditions.
### **Precision Systems for Refractory & Materials Testing**
Our materials and [refractory testing](https://www.kilns.co.uk/kilns/test-kilns) kilns and furnaces are engineered to deliver uniform heat distribution and stable thermal performance, allowing repeatable and reliable results in every testing cycle.
Using advanced insulation materials, precision temperature monitoring, and computer-aided control systems, these furnaces maintain strict temperature tolerances while supporting a wide range of high-temperature testing procedures. Each unit is suitable for both batch and continuous testing environments, ensuring flexibility for small-scale laboratory trials or full-scale industrial evaluation.
### **Testing Applications & Capabilities**
Our [high temperature materials testing](https://www.kilns.co.uk/kilns/test-kilns) systems are designed to support multiple processes, including thermal shock testing, creep testing, mechanical strength evaluation, chemical resistance testing, and stress-relieving cycles.
Whether assessing firebricks, ceramic components, or heat-resistant alloys, our kilns and furnaces provide the controlled environment necessary for consistent, high-precision results. Systems can be customised with multi-zone temperature control, atmosphere regulation, and full data logging for accurate process recording and analysis.
### **Built for Performance & Compliance**
All materials testing furnaces are manufactured to meet UKCA, CE, and BS EN 746 standards. Their robust construction and energy-efficient design ensure long-term reliability, while advanced control systems maintain precise temperature uniformity throughout each test cycle. Each furnace is tailored to the client’s specific testing requirements, whether for extreme high-temperature exposure, thermal cycling, or controlled atmosphere conditions.
Our team works closely with laboratories and industrial partners to design kilns and furnaces that match precise chamber sizes, thermal profiles, and operational workflows, ensuring repeatable and reliable testing outcomes.
### **Why Choose Kilns & Furnaces?**
– Over 70 years of expertise in high-temperature kiln and furnace design.  
– Proven performance across refractory, ceramics, and advanced materials testing.  
– Custom materials testing equipment built to your exact specifications.  
– Full UK-based installation, support, and maintenance services.
### **Bespoke Refractory & Materials Testing Solutions**
Whether you require a dedicated refractory testing kiln, a high-precision materials testing furnace, or a full laboratory testing system, our team can design and manufacture a solution tailored to your testing protocols, material types, and operational requirements.
Enquire with our specialists today to discuss your testing needs or [request a bespoke quotation](https://www.kilns.co.uk/contact-us).

# Education Kilns for UK Schools, Colleges & Universities
## A practical guide for teachers, technicians and procurement teams
Choosing the right education kiln depends on what you plan to fire, how often it will be used, the available space and electrical supply. Kilns & Furnaces manufactures education kilns for schools, colleges and universities, from compact ceramics kilns to larger front-loading and specialist systems.

## What to consider before you buy an education kiln
### 1) What will you fire (and to what temperature)?
The right kiln depends heavily on what you teach and produce:
  * KS3 / GCSE ceramics typically needs dependable bisque and glaze cycles.
  * A-Level / BTEC / HE often benefits from higher temperature capability and more advanced firing schedules (ramps, soaks and controlled cooling).
  * Many departments also run test tiles, decals, and specialist materials for experimentation and assessment.  
We are able to recommend a kiln specification based on your curriculum level and intended outcomes.


### 2) Throughput (how busy the kiln will be)
In education, capacity is rarely “nice to have”, it affects your timetable:
  * If the kiln is too small, it becomes a bottleneck and creates backlogs.
  * If it’s oversized, it can be harder to schedule and less efficient for small batches.
  * The best fit is usually a kiln that supports normal weekly output comfortably, with enough flexibility for peak periods such as exam projects, clubs and end-of-term work.


### 3) Loading style and day-to-day usability
Loading style changes workflow, accessibility and safety:
  * Top-loading kilns are widely used in schools and studios for general ceramics work and smaller footprints.
  * Front-loading kilns can offer improved visibility and easier access for loading/unloading shelves and larger pieces.
  * Easy-load / roll-out hearth kilns reduce bending and reaching, making them particularly useful for frequent firings and larger work in colleges and universities.
  * If technicians do most loading, ergonomics and access can make a big difference over a school year. If students may load under supervision, visibility and safe access are especially important.


### 4) Power supply and installation considerations
Kilns are only straightforward when the site’s electrics and layout support them. We may ask you about:
  * Single phase vs three phase
  * Available amperage
  * The location of isolators and safe cable routes
  * Space, clearance and access for delivery/positioning
  * Whether the kiln room can manage heat and ventilation effectively


We will help you navigate this early so you can avoid delays once your budgets are approved.
### 5) Safety and risk controls in education settings
A safe kiln room needs more than good intentions. Your setup should support:
  * Safe siting (clearances and heat-safe surroundings)
  * Suitable safety interlocks and temperature protection (where applicable)
  * Controlled access in shared spaces (workshops, corridors, open studios)
  * Clear operating procedures and supervision rules


* * *
## Which kiln type suits your department?
### For secondary schools and sixth forms
For curriculum ceramics, many departments choose education-focused top loaders or compact front loaders, depending on available space and how the room is laid out.
### For FE colleges (higher throughput)
Front-loading kilns can be a strong fit for busy departments, particularly where accessibility and consistent loading matters across multiple staff and groups.
### For universities and specialist pottery schools
If you’re firing larger sculptural work, running frequent cycles, or needing greater workflow efficiency, larger front-loaders and easy-load / roll-out hearth options can improve handling and reduce strain.
### For jewellery, enamels, small tests and technician-led work
A bench-mounted kiln can be ideal where controlled smaller firings are needed without dedicating a large footprint.
### Controllers: consistent results that students can learn from
In education, repeatability is essential. A good controller helps you:
  * Standardise firings across classes
  * Reduce faults caused by inconsistent ramps/cooling
  * Teach firing fundamentals (ramp rate, soak, controlled cooling, glaze maturity)


If you run varied programmes, it’s usually worth choosing a controller that supports multiple schedules and logging.
Controller info: [kilns.co.uk/controllers](https://www.kilns.co.uk/controllers)
* * *
## Ventilation, siting and safer kiln rooms
Even electric kilns produce heat and can release fumes from clay bodies, glazes, decals, binders and classroom materials. A well-planned kiln space typically includes:
  * Ventilation suited to the room and firing profile
  * Clear, heat-safe zones around the kiln
  * Extraction solutions where required
  * A layout that supports safe supervision and controlled access
  * Learn more about Heat and fume canopies: [kilns.co.uk/kilns/heat-and-fume-collection-canopy](https://www.kilns.co.uk/kilns/heat-and-fume-collection-canopy)
  * Learn more about Heat locks: [kilns.co.uk/kilns/heat-lock](https://www.kilns.co.uk/kilns/heat-lock)

When you contact us, we may ask a few practical questions to recommend the best model. Common topics include:
  * Your education setting (school/college/university/specialist studio)
  * What you’ll be firing (bisque/glaze/stoneware/tests/decals)
  * Your required maximum temperature

  * Available space and access for installation

  * Timescale for delivery/installation

## FAQs
### What’s the best kiln for a school ceramics classroom?
The best kiln is one that suits your firing temperature needs, fits safely in your space, and supports the amount of student work you produce each week.
### Do we need three-phase power for a kiln?
Not always. It depends on kiln size and power rating—many education settings can run suitable models on available supplies.
### Top-loader or front-loader for education?
Top-loaders can be space-efficient and versatile. Front-loaders can offer easier access and visibility. The best choice depends on your room layout and workflow.
### Should we plan ventilation?
Yes. Heat management and ventilation are important in any kiln room, especially where a range of clays, glazes and materials are used.
### How do we choose the right size?
A properly sized kiln should comfortably handle typical weekly class output, with enough flexibility for peak periods such as exam projects and clubs.

19th October 2021 | [News](https://www.kilns.co.uk/category/news)
![](https://www.kilns.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/Small-Furnace5.png)
Introducing our CU Labtech Kiln. Ideal for our industrial grade clients, enabling them to test fire without needing a large kiln.
The Labtech is a front loading test kiln constructed of a low thermal mass insulation brick with a high grade backup insulation board enclosed within an electrostatic powder coated cabinet.
The CU Labtech comes with a Eurotherm 3216 controller.
The Eurotherm 3216 controller comes with several advanced features that are not available in similar controllers. The 3216 provides precision control of process variables like temperature.The 3216 is quick and easy to commission – no need for expert knowledge. Clear information of process with scrolling, custom messages. Custom alarm messages for easy understanding. Recipe selection from operator interface. Internal timer and set point programming. Instant indication of heater faults with integral ammeter. Remote set point – solution for multi-zone applications
Features:
  * Remote set point


  * Heater failure detection


  * Current monitoring


  * Internal timer


  * Scrolling text messages


  * Modbus comms


  * Type approved to EN14597 TR


  * 8 Segment programmer


  * Modbus SP retransmission


  * Help text


  * Recipes


  * Analogue retransmission
  * Multi-language support (English, German, French, Italian and Spanish)


The Labtech is suitable for heat treatment, ceramics, bricks, tiles and glass. If you would like more information on how the Labtech kiln can add value to your business, our team is happy to help! Please email sales@kilns.co.uk

# Create and Craft with Kilns & Furnaces’ Phoenix Hobby Kiln
6th March 2024 | [News](https://www.kilns.co.uk/category/news)
![Kilns and Furnaces Phoenix Hobby Kiln. Our best-selling, best value small kiln.](https://www.kilns.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/Phoenix-Kiln-Promo_Blog-Image.jpg)
[The Phoenix](https://www.kilns.co.uk/kilns/phoenix-range) is a compact 38-litre hobby kiln designed for pottery, ceramics and small-scale firing. Operating from a 13 A UK supply, it provides an accessible option for home studios, hobby potters and makers looking for a small, practical kiln.
## Safety First:
One of the standout features of the Phoenix Kiln is its commitment to safety. Crafted with a square firing chamber for maximum setting density, the Phoenix Kiln ensures efficient use of space while minimizing risks during operation. The electrical lid safety system adds an extra layer of security, reducing the chance of accidents and allowing you to focus on your craft without worry.
## All-Round Performance:
With a maximum operating temperature of 1260°C, this kiln is ready to bring your pottery visions to life. The durable low thermal mass brick construction ensures efficiency, while the high-grade back-up insulation and efficient low thermal mass brickwork contribute to its high levels of performance. Like all of our kilns, the Phoenix is equipped with a Type R thermocouple and high-grade spiral wound elements, the Phoenix Kiln also features a lid safety switch compliant with current safety regulations and over-temperature protection. The inclusion of lockable castor wheels and a 13 AMP plug suitable for all UK domestic sockets adds to its user-friendly design, making it easy to set up and use right away.
## Versatility Built-In:
The Phoenix Kiln offers more than just safety and efficiency – it provides versatility to cater the specific needs required of your craft. With an instrument socket ready to accept all controllers in our range, you have the option to customize your operating settings. Additionally, Kilns & Furnaces offer optional features such as the ST215C digital control system, and additional kiln furniture allowing you to take full control of your firing process.
## In Stock and Available for Delivery:
Our Phoenix Kilns are in stock and available for both UK and International delivery. We understand that a kiln is a vital part of your hobby or business, and we want to ensure that you can fire-up your wares without delay.
## Technical Specifications:
Capacity: 38 litres / 1.34 cu ft  
Firing Chamber Dimensions: 330mm Diameter x 330mm Height  
Overall Dimensions: 490mm Width x 590mm Depth x 675mm Height  
Weight: 50 kg / 110 lb  
Power Supply: 3 KW, 240V, 13A
## Optional Features:
We offer optional features such as the ST215C digital control system and a special element design for low-temperature ceramic applications. Simply contact us to discuss your unique requirements.

# Meet Our Drawing Office Manager | Dave Cotton
4th September 2024 | [News](https://www.kilns.co.uk/category/news)
![Meet Dave Cotton, our drawing office manager.](https://www.kilns.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/Dave_Drawing-Office-Manager_v1_Blog-Image.jpg)
At Kilns & Furnaces, our success is built on quality and expertise, and few exemplify this better than Dave Cotton, our longest-serving Drawing Office Manager with over 50 years of dedicated service. Today, we want to highlight Dave’s invaluable contributions and delve into the kiln design process he has perfected over the years, enriched by a lifetime of diverse engineering experience.
## **A Lifetime of Engineering Mastery**
Dave’s journey in engineering began in 1961 at Stanfield Technical High School in Stoke-on-Trent, where he studied multiple engineering disciplines, mastering both the practical and theoretical elements of the field. His fascination with how things are constructed, their materials, and the qualities they bring to the final product naturally led him into the world of design engineering.
Starting his career at the age of 16 as a Draughtsman, Dave’s early work spanned a variety of fields—from sewage works and artificial hearts to air conditioning systems and submarines. These experiences gave him a broad understanding of engineering applications, which he brought with him when he joined Kilns & Furnaces mid-1970’s.
## **The Evolution of Kiln Design**
While the kiln design process has evolved significantly over the decades, the core principles—efficiency, durability, and precision—remain unchanged. Dave has consistently upheld these values, ensuring that innovation never compromises the essentials of good design.
Dave’s career has spanned significant transformations in British engineering, from the introduction of the metric system in the 1970s to the transition from hand-drawn designs to computer-aided design (CAD). By the age of 20, he was already working through the paper-to-digital transformation, using early technologies like dot matrix plotters. As the industry advanced, so did Dave, seamlessly transitioning to innovative programmes such as Generic CADD and, to this day, leveraging tools like VisualCAD.
## **Marrying Tradition with Technology**
Despite the technological advancements, Dave’s design process begins with a traditional approach—starting with pencil and paper. This method, refined over decades, allows him to visualise the kiln’s structure in its simplest, most practical form. His artistic talent shines through in these initial sketches, where his keen eye for detail ensures that every design is grounded in craftsmanship.
Once the concept is sketched, Dave transitions to advanced design software, refining his ideas with precision. This blend of tradition and modern technology enables him to create bespoke industrial solutions tailored to specific client needs.
## **Commitment to Quality and Client Satisfaction**
Dave’s contributions go beyond technical expertise; his deep understanding of kiln operation and client requirements ensures that each design is both technically sound and practically effective. Whether developing standard models or bespoke solutions, Dave’s designs consistently deliver long-term value and enhance our clients’ operations.
His foresight in addressing potential challenges during the design phase has saved countless hours in production and installation, significantly contributing to the efficiency and success of our projects. Dave’s unwavering commitment to quality makes him an invaluable member of our team and a trusted partner to our clients.
## **Looking Ahead**
As we move forward, the field of kiln design will continue to evolve, with new technologies and environmental considerations playing a key role. With experienced professionals like Dave, Kilns & Furnaces is well-positioned to continue delivering innovative, high-quality kiln solutions.
We extend our heartfelt thanks to Dave for his outstanding service and dedication. His expertise is a cornerstone of our success.

## Metal Heat Treatment Furnaces
At [Kilns & Furnaces](https://www.kilns.co.uk/), we design and manufacture high-performance metal heat treatment furnaces engineered to meet the demanding requirements of modern manufacturing, engineering, and industrial production. With over 70 years of experience, our [heat treatment furnaces](https://www.kilns.co.uk/kilns/heat-treatment-kilns) deliver precision temperature control, durability, and efficiency for a wide range of metallurgical processes, from annealing and hardening to tempering and stress relieving.
### Precision Furnaces for Metal Applications
Our heat treatment furnaces are built to provide consistent, uniform heat distribution and excellent thermal stability, ensuring repeatable results in every production cycle. We combine advanced insulation materials, accurate temperature monitoring, and computer-aided control systems to deliver furnaces that perform reliably under continuous industrial use.
Designed with versatility in mind, our metal heat treatment furnaces enable a wide range of processes, within a single, high-performance system. Each unit maintains precise temperature control and efficient heat transfer, ensuring metallurgical accuracy and dependable results across all stages of production.
### **Furnace Applications & Capabilities**
Our metal heat treatment systems support a wide range of industrial processes, including:
  * **Annealing** : Controlled heating and slow cooling to reduce hardness and improve workability.
  * **Hardening** : High-temperature heating followed by rapid quenching to increase material strength.
  * **Tempering** : Reheating hardened metals to improve toughness and reduce brittleness.
  * **Stress Relieving** : Removing residual stresses after machining or welding to enhance stability.


Our furnaces can be configured for batch or continuous production environments, with flexible chamber sizes, atmosphere control, and data logging options available.
### **Built for Performance & Compliance**
Each metal heat treatment furnace we produce is engineered to meet international safety and performance standards, including BS EN 746, UKCA, and CE compliance. Energy-efficient design, robust construction, and precision control ensure optimal performance, reduced operating costs, and consistent product quality. Our team works closely with clients to meet specific process requirements, from temperature uniformity and atmosphere control to integration with existing factory systems.
### **Why Choose Kilns & Furnaces?**
– Over 70 years of industry experience in kiln and furnace design.  
– Proven performance across aerospace, automotive, engineering, and manufacturing sectors.  
– Bespoke solutions tailored to your heat treatment process.  
– Full UK-based support, maintenance, and spare parts service.
### Bespoke Heat Treatment Furnaces
Whether you require a bespoke metal heat treatment furnace, a precision annealing furnace, or a robust hardening or tempering furnace, our team at Kilns & Furnaces can design a system tailored to your exact process and performance needs.
We’ll work closely with you to specify the right configuration, controls, and compliance features for your production environment. Speak to our specialists today to discuss your requirements and [request a quote](https://www.kilns.co.uk/contact-us).
